sanskrit: śaktiṃ visṛjya rādheyaḥ puraṃdara ivāśanim nanāda sumahānādaṃ balavān sūtanandanaḥ taṃ ca nādaṃ tataḥ śrutvā putrās te hṛṣitābhavan
english: Having hurled the spear as Puraṃdara hurls the thunderbolt, the mighty son of the sūta, Rādheya, roared a tremendous roar; and hearing that roar your sons were filled with joy.

sanskrit: tāṃ karṇabhujanirmuktām arkavaiśvānaraprabhām śaktiṃ viyati ciccheda bhīmaḥ saptabhir āśugaiḥ
english: That spear loosed from Karṇa's arm, blazing like the sun and like fire, Bhīma cut to pieces in mid-air with seven swift arrows.

sanskrit: chittvā śaktiṃ tato bhīmo nirmuktoragasaṃnibhām mārgamāṇa iva prāṇān sūtaputrasya māriṣa
english: Having shattered that spear, which resembled a serpent freed from its slough, Bhīma then, O venerable one, as though seeking out the very life-breath of the son of the sūta,

sanskrit: prāhiṇon nava saṃrabdhaḥ śarān barhiṇavāsasaḥ svarṇapuṅkhāñ śilādhautān yamadaṇḍopamān mṛdhe
english: in his fury sent forth in battle nine arrows fledged with peacock plumes, gold-shafted, whetted upon stone, like to the rod of Yama.

sanskrit: karṇo 'py anyad dhanur gṛhya hemapṛṣṭhaṃ durāsadam vikṛṣya ca mahātejā vyasṛjat sāyakān nava
english: Karṇa too, taking up another bow, gold-backed and hard to withstand, and drawing it, that mighty-splendored one let fly nine shafts.

sanskrit: tān pāṇḍuputraś ciccheda navabhir nataparvabhiḥ vasuṣeṇena nirmuktān nava rājan mahāśarān chittvā bhīmo mahārāja nādaṃ siṃha ivānadat
english: Those the son of Pāṇḍu cut apart with nine smooth-jointed shafts; and having severed the nine great arrows loosed by Vasuṣeṇa, O great king, Bhīma roared as a lion roars.

sanskrit: tau vṛṣāv iva nardantau balinau vāśitāntare śārdūlāv iva cānyonyam atyarthaṃ ca hy agarjatām
english: The two mighty ones, bellowing like bulls over a cow in heat, roared exceedingly at one another like two tigers.

sanskrit: anyonyaṃ prajihīrṣantāv anyonyasyāntaraiṣiṇau anyonyam abhivīkṣantau goṣṭheṣv iva maharṣabhau
english: Each longing to strike the other, each watching for the other's opening, they glared at one another like two great bulls in the cattle-pens.

sanskrit: mahāgajāv ivāsādya viṣāṇāgraiḥ parasparam śaraiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: Closing like two great elephants goring each other with the tips of their tusks, they smote one another with arrows loosed from bows drawn to the full.

sanskrit: nirdahantau mahārāja śaravṛṣṭyā parasparam anyonyam abhivīkṣantau kopād vivṛtalocanau
english: Scorching each other, O great king, with showers of arrows, they glared at one another, their eyes wide open in wrath.

sanskrit: prahasantau tathānyonyaṃ bhartsayantau muhur muhuḥ śaṅkhaśabdaṃ ca kurvāṇau yuyudhāte parasparam
english: Laughing at one another and taunting each other again and again, sounding their conches the while, they fought together.

sanskrit: tasya bhīmaḥ punaś cāpaṃ muṣṭau ciccheda māriṣa śaṅkhavarṇāś ca tān aśvān bāṇair ninye yamakṣayam
english: Once more Bhīma cut his bow asunder at the grip, O venerable one, and with his arrows sent his conch-white horses to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tathā kṛcchragataṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ duryodhano nṛpaḥ vepamāna iva krodhād vyādideśātha durjayam
english: Seeing Karṇa thus brought to straits, King Duryodhana, trembling as it were with rage, then gave command to Durjaya:

sanskrit: gaccha durjaya rādheyaṃ purā grasati pāṇḍavaḥ jahi tūbarakaṃ kṣipraṃ karṇasya balam ādadhat
english: "Go, Durjaya, before the Pāṇḍava devours Rādheya; swiftly slay this hornless one and lend your strength to Karṇa."

sanskrit: evam uktas tathety uktvā tava putras tavātmajam abhyadravad bhīmasenaṃ vyāsaktaṃ vikirañ śarān
english: Thus addressed, your son answered "So be it," and rushed upon Bhīmasena, who was engaged elsewhere, scattering arrows as he came.

sanskrit: sa bhīmaṃ navabhir bāṇair aśvān aṣṭabhir ardayat ṣaḍbhiḥ sūtaṃ tribhiḥ ketuṃ punas taṃ cāpi saptabhiḥ
english: He afflicted Bhīma with nine arrows, his horses with eight, his driver with six, his standard with three, and Bhīma again with seven.

sanskrit: bhīmaseno 'pi saṃkruddhaḥ sāśvayantāram āśugaiḥ durjayaṃ bhinnamarmāṇam anayad yamasādanam
english: Bhīmasena too, greatly enraged, with his swift shafts pierced Durjaya in his vitals and, horses and charioteer with him, sent him to the dwelling of Yama.

sanskrit: svalaṃkṛtaṃ kṣitau kṣuṇṇaṃ ceṣṭamānaṃ yathoragam rudann ārtas tava sutaṃ karṇaś cakre pradakṣiṇam
english: As your richly adorned son lay crushed upon the earth, writhing like a serpent, Karṇa, weeping and stricken with grief, made a reverent circuit about him.

sanskrit: sa tu taṃ virathaṃ kṛtvā smayann atyantavairiṇam samācinod bāṇagaṇaiḥ śataghnīm iva śaṅkubhiḥ
english: But Bhīma, having stripped his bitter foe of his chariot, smiling, covered him over with masses of arrows as a śataghnī is studded with spikes.

sanskrit: tathāpy atirathaḥ karṇo bhidyamānaḥ sma sāyakaiḥ na jahau samare bhīmaṃ kruddharūpaṃ paraṃtapaḥ
english: Yet even so the mighty car-warrior Karṇa, that scorcher of foes, though pierced through by the shafts, did not abandon the wrathful-visaged Bhīma in the fight.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca sa tathā virathaḥ karṇaḥ punar bhīmena nirjitaḥ ratham anyaṃ samāsthāya sadyo vivyādha pāṇḍavam
english: Saṃjaya said: Karṇa, thus deprived of his chariot and again vanquished by Bhīma, mounting another car, straightway pierced the Pāṇḍava.

sanskrit: mahāgajāv ivāsādya viṣāṇāgraiḥ parasparam śaraiḥ pūrṇāyatotsṛṣṭair anyonyam abhijaghnatuḥ
english: Closing like two great elephants goring each other with the tips of their tusks, they smote one another with arrows loosed from bows drawn to the full.

sanskrit: atha karṇaḥ śaravrātair bhīmaṃ balavad ardayat nanāda balavan nādaṃ punar vivyādha corasi
english: Then Karṇa afflicted Bhīma sorely with multitudes of arrows, roared a mighty roar, and again pierced him in the chest.

sanskrit: taṃ bhīmo daśabhir bāṇaiḥ pratyavidhyad ajihmagaiḥ punar vivyādha viṃśatyā śarāṇāṃ nataparvaṇām
english: Bhīma pierced him back with ten straight-flying arrows, and pierced him again with twenty smooth-jointed shafts.

sanskrit: karṇas tu navabhir bhīmaṃ viddhvā rājan stanāntare dhvajam ekena vivyādha sāyakena śitena ha
english: But Karṇa, O king, having pierced Bhīma with nine arrows between the breasts, pierced his standard with a single keen shaft.

sanskrit: sāyakānāṃ tataḥ pārthas triṣaṣṭyā pratyavidhyata tottrair iva mahānāgaṃ kaśābhir iva vājinam
english: Then the son of Pṛthā pierced him in return with sixty-three shafts, as a great elephant is goaded with hooks, or a horse with whips.

sanskrit: so 'tividdho mahārāja pāṇḍavena yaśasvinā sṛkviṇī lelihan vīraḥ krodhasaṃraktalocanaḥ
english: Sorely pierced, O great king, by the illustrious Pāṇḍava, that hero, licking the corners of his mouth, his eyes red with wrath,

sanskrit: tataḥ śaraṃ mahārāja sarvakāyāvadāraṇam prāhiṇod bhīmasenāya balāyendra ivāśanim
english: then, O great king, loosed at Bhīmasena an arrow that could rend any body, as Indra hurls the thunderbolt against the Daityas.

sanskrit: sa nirbhidya raṇe pārthaṃ sūtaputradhanuścyutaḥ agacchad dārayan bhūmiṃ citrapuṅkhaḥ śilīmukhaḥ
english: That gaily-feathered shaft, loosed from the sūta's son's bow, having pierced the son of Pṛthā in battle, passed on and split the ground.

sanskrit: sarvaśaikyāṃ catuṣkiṣkuṃ gurvīṃ rukmāṅgadāṃ gadām prāhiṇot sūtaputrāya ṣaḍasrām avicārayan
english: Without hesitation Bhīma hurled at the sūta's son a heavy mace, wholly of iron, four cubits long, banded with gold and six-edged.

sanskrit: tayā jaghānādhiratheḥ sadaśvān sādhuvāhinaḥ gadayā bhārataḥ kruddho vajreṇendra ivāsurān
english: With that mace the wrathful Bhārata slew the goodly, well-trained steeds of the son of Adhiratha, as Indra slew the Asuras with the thunderbolt.

sanskrit: tato bhīmo mahābāhuḥ kṣurābhyāṃ bharatarṣabha dhvajam ādhiratheś chittvā sūtam abhyahanat tadā
english: Then the mighty-armed Bhīma, O bull of the Bharatas, with two razor-edged arrows cut down the standard of Adhiratha's son and struck down his charioteer.

sanskrit: hatāśvasūtam utsṛjya rathaṃ sa patitadhvajam visphārayan dhanuḥ karṇas tasthau bhārata durmanāḥ
english: Forsaking the car whose horses and driver were slain and whose standard had fallen, Karṇa, twanging his bow, stood there, O Bhārata, downcast in heart.

sanskrit: tatrādbhutam apaśyāma rādheyasya parākramam viratho rathināṃ śreṣṭho vārayām āsa yad ripum
english: There we beheld a wondrous feat of Rādheya's prowess: bereft of his chariot, that best of car-warriors yet held his enemy at bay.

sanskrit: virathaṃ taṃ rathaśreṣṭhaṃ dṛṣṭvādhirathim āhave duryodhanas tato rājann abhyabhāṣata durmukham
english: Seeing the son of Adhiratha, that foremost of car-warriors, deprived of his car in the battle, Duryodhana then, O king, spoke to Durmukha:

sanskrit: eṣa durmukha rādheyo bhīmena virathīkṛtaḥ taṃ rathena naraśreṣṭhaṃ saṃpādaya mahāratham
english: "This Rādheya, O Durmukha, has been stripped of his chariot by Bhīma; furnish that best of men, that mighty car-warrior, with a car."

sanskrit: duryodhanavacaḥ śrutvā tato bhārata durmukhaḥ tvaramāṇo 'byayāt karṇaṃ bhīmaṃ cāvārayac charaiḥ
english: Hearing Duryodhana's word, O Bhārata, Durmukha hastened to Karṇa and held Bhīma off with arrows.

sanskrit: durmukhaṃ prekṣya saṃgrāme sūtaputrapadānugam vāyuputraḥ prahṛṣṭo 'bhūt sṛkkiṇī parilelihan
english: Beholding Durmukha in the fray hastening to the side of the sūta's son, the son of Vāyu rejoiced, licking the corners of his mouth.

sanskrit: tataḥ karṇaṃ mahārāja vārayitvā śilīmukhaiḥ durmukhāya rathaṃ śīghraṃ preṣayām āsa pāṇḍavaḥ
english: Then, O great king, having warded off Karṇa with his arrows, the Pāṇḍava swiftly drove his car toward Durmukha.

sanskrit: tasmin kṣaṇe mahārāja navabhir nataparvabhiḥ supuṅkhair durmukhaṃ bhīmaḥ śarair ninye yamakṣayam
english: In that instant, O great king, with nine well-feathered, smooth-jointed shafts Bhīma sent Durmukha to the abode of Yama.

sanskrit: tatas tam evādhirathiḥ syandanaṃ durmukhe hate āsthitaḥ prababhau rājan dīpyamāna ivāṃśumān
english: Then, Durmukha being slain, the son of Adhiratha mounted that very car and shone, O king, like the radiant sun.

sanskrit: śayānaṃ bhinnamarmāṇaṃ durmukhaṃ śoṇitokṣitam dṛṣṭvā karṇo 'śrupūrṇākṣo muhūrtaṃ nābhyavartata
english: Seeing Durmukha lying with his vitals pierced and bathed in blood, Karṇa, his eyes filled with tears, for a moment did not advance.

sanskrit: taṃ gatāsum atikramya kṛtvā karṇaḥ pradakṣiṇam dīrgham uṣṇaṃ śvasan vīro na kiṃ cit pratyapadyata
english: Passing by the lifeless one and making a reverent circuit about him, the hero Karṇa, sighing long and hot, could do nothing at all.

sanskrit: tasmiṃs tu vivare rājan nārācān gārdhravāsasaḥ prāhiṇot sūtaputrāya bhīmasenaś caturdaśa
english: In that opening, O king, Bhīmasena loosed at the sūta's son fourteen iron arrows fledged with vulture-feathers.

sanskrit: te tasya kavacaṃ bhittvā svarṇapuṅkhā mahaujasaḥ hemacitrā mahārāja dyotayanto diśo daśa
english: Those gold-shafted, exceedingly powerful arrows, splendidly wrought with gold, O great king, having pierced his armor, lit up the ten directions,

sanskrit: apiban sūtaputrasya śoṇitaṃ raktabhojanāḥ kruddhā iva manuṣyendra bhujagāḥ kālacoditāḥ
english: and, feeding upon blood, drank the blood of the sūta's son, O lord of men, like enraged serpents urged on by Death.

sanskrit: prasarpamāṇā medinyāṃ te vyarocanta mārgaṇāḥ ardhapraviṣṭāḥ saṃrabdhā bilānīva mahoragāḥ
english: Gliding upon the earth, those shafts shone forth as, half-entered into their holes, great serpents furiously dart.

sanskrit: taṃ pratyavidhyad rādheyo jāmbūnadavibhūṣitaiḥ caturdaśabhir aty ugrair nārācair avicārayan
english: Rādheya pierced him in return, without hesitation, with fourteen exceedingly fierce iron arrows adorned with gold.

sanskrit: te bhīmasenasya bhujaṃ savyaṃ nirbhidya patriṇaḥ prāviśan medinīṃ bhīmāḥ krauñcaṃ patrarathā iva
english: Those terrible winged shafts, having pierced through Bhīmasena's left arm, entered the earth as birds plunge into the Krauñca mountain.

sanskrit: te vyarocanta nārācāḥ praviśanto vasuṃdharām gacchaty astaṃ dinakare dīpyamānā ivāṃśavaḥ
english: Those iron arrows, entering the earth, shone like the blazing rays of the day-maker as he goes to his setting.

sanskrit: sa nirbhinno raṇe bhīmo nārācair marmabhedibhiḥ susrāva rudhiraṃ bhūri parvataḥ salilaṃ yathā
english: Bhīma, pierced in battle by those vital-rending iron arrows, streamed forth blood in abundance as a mountain pours down water.

sanskrit: sa bhīmas tribhir āyastaḥ sūtaputraṃ patatribhiḥ suparṇavegair vivyādha sārathiṃ cāsya saptabhiḥ
english: That Bhīma, stretched to his utmost, pierced the sūta's son with three winged shafts swift as Suparṇa, and his charioteer with seven.

sanskrit: sa vihvalo mahārāja karṇo bhīmabalārditaḥ prādravaj javanair aśvai raṇaṃ hitvā mahāyaśāḥ
english: Reeling, O great king, and sore afflicted by Bhīma's might, the illustrious Karṇa abandoned the battle and fled away with his swift horses.

sanskrit: bhīmasenas tu visphārya cāpaṃ hemapariṣkṛtam āhave 'tiratho 'tiṣṭhaj jvalann iva hutāśanaḥ
english: But Bhīmasena, twanging his gold-decked bow, that mighty car-warrior stood in the battle blazing like the fire that devours offerings.

sanskrit: dhṛtarāṣṭra uvāca daivam eva paraṃ manye dhik pauruṣam anarthakam yatrādhirathir āyasto nātarat pāṇḍavaṃ raṇe
english: Dhṛtarāṣṭra said: Fate, I deem, is supreme; fie upon human effort, that comes to naught, since the son of Adhiratha, straining his utmost, could not overcome the Pāṇḍava in battle.

sanskrit: karṇaḥ pārthān sagovindāñ jetum utsahate raṇe na ca karṇasamaṃ yodhaṃ loke paśyāmi kaṃ cana iti duryodhanasyāham aśrauṣaṃ jalpato muhuḥ
english: "Karṇa is able to conquer the sons of Pṛthā together with Govinda in battle, and I see no warrior in the world equal to Karṇa" — thus did I hear Duryodhana prate again and again.

sanskrit: karṇo hi balavāñ śūro dṛḍhadhanvā jitaklamaḥ iti mām abravīt sūta mando duryodhanaḥ purā
english: "For Karṇa is mighty, a hero, firm of bow, conqueror of fatigue" — thus the foolish Duryodhana spoke to me of old, O sūta.

sanskrit: vasuṣeṇasahāyaṃ māṃ nālaṃ devāpi saṃyuge kim u pāṇḍusutā rājan gatasattvā vicetasaḥ
english: "With Vasuṣeṇa for my ally, not even the gods are a match for me in war, O king — how much less the sons of Pāṇḍu, drained of strength and bereft of sense."

sanskrit: tatra taṃ nirjitaṃ dṛṣṭvā bhujaṃgam iva nirviṣam yuddhāt karṇam apakrāntaṃ kiṃ svid duryodhano 'bravīt
english: Now, seeing Karṇa there vanquished, like a serpent drained of its venom, withdrawn from the fight — what, pray, did Duryodhana say?

sanskrit: aho durmukham evaikaṃ yuddhānām aviśāradam prāveśayad dhutavahaṃ pataṃgam iva mohitaḥ
english: Alas, in his bewilderment he sent Durmukha alone, unskilled in warfare, into the battle, as a moth is sent into the fire.

sanskrit: aśvatthāmā madrarājaḥ kṛpaḥ karṇaś ca saṃgatāḥ na śaktāḥ pramukhe sthātuṃ nūnaṃ bhīmasya saṃjaya
english: Aśvatthāman, the king of the Madras, Kṛpa, and Karṇa, even joined together, are surely unable to stand before Bhīma, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: te 'pi cāsya mahāghoraṃ balaṃ nāgāyutopamam jānanto vyavasāyaṃ ca krūraṃ mārutatejasaḥ
english: They too, knowing his most terrible strength, like that of ten thousand elephants, and the cruel resolve of that one whose splendor is the Wind's,

sanskrit: kimarthaṃ krūrakarmāṇaṃ yamakālāntakopamam balasaṃrambhavīryajñāḥ kopayiṣyanti saṃyuge
english: why, knowing his might, his fury, and his valor, would they provoke in battle that one of cruel deeds, who is like Yama, Time, and the Ender?

sanskrit: karṇas tv eko mahābāhuḥ svabāhubalam āśritaḥ bhīmasenam anādṛtya raṇe 'yudhyata sūtajaḥ
english: Yet Karṇa alone, the mighty-armed son of the sūta, relying on the strength of his own arms, made light of Bhīmasena and fought him in battle.

sanskrit: yo 'jayat samare karṇaṃ puraṃdara ivāsuram na sa pāṇḍusuto jetuṃ śakyaḥ kena cid āhave
english: He who vanquished Karṇa in battle as Puraṃdara vanquished the Asura — that son of Pāṇḍu can be conquered by none in the fight.

sanskrit: droṇaṃ yaḥ saṃpramathyaikaḥ praviṣṭo mama vāhinīm bhīmo dhanaṃjayānveṣī kas tam archej jijīviṣuḥ
english: Bhīma, who, crushing Droṇa, alone penetrated my host in search of Dhanaṃjaya — who that wished to live would withstand him?

sanskrit: ko hi saṃjaya bhīmasya sthātum utsahate 'grataḥ udyatāśanivajrasya mahendrasyeva dānavaḥ
english: For who, O Saṃjaya, would dare to stand before Bhīma, as a Dānava before great Indra with his thunderbolt upraised?

sanskrit: pretarājapuraṃ prāpya nivartetāpi mānavaḥ na bhīmasenaṃ saṃprāpya nivarteta kadā cana
english: A man might come even to the city of the king of the dead and return, but having come upon Bhīmasena he would never return.

sanskrit: pataṃgā iva vahniṃ te prāviśann alpacetasaḥ ye bhīmasenaṃ saṃkruddham abhyadhāvan vimohitāḥ
english: Like moths into the fire those dull-witted ones plunged, who in their bewilderment rushed against the wrathful Bhīmasena.

sanskrit: yat tat sabhāyāṃ bhīmena mama putravadhāśrayam śaptaṃ saṃrambhiṇogreṇa kurūṇāṃ śṛṇvatāṃ tadā
english: That oath which Bhīma swore in the assembly, touching the slaughter of my sons, the fierce and furious one, in the hearing of the Kurus then —

sanskrit: tan nūnam abhisaṃcintya dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ ca nirjitam duḥśāsanaḥ saha bhrātrā bhayād bhīmād upāramat
english: surely remembering that, and seeing Karṇa vanquished, Duḥśāsana with his brother drew back from Bhīma out of fear.

sanskrit: yaś ca saṃjaya durbuddhir abravīt samitau muhuḥ karṇo duḥśāsano 'haṃ ca jeṣyāmo yudhi pāṇḍavān
english: And he of evil mind, O Saṃjaya, who said again and again in the council, "Karṇa, Duḥśāsana, and I shall conquer the Pāṇḍavas in battle" —

sanskrit: sa nūnaṃ virathaṃ dṛṣṭvā karṇaṃ bhīmena nirjitam pratyākhyānāc ca kṛṣṇasya bhṛśaṃ tapyati saṃjaya
english: he, surely, seeing Karṇa stripped of his car and vanquished by Bhīma, and recalling his rejection of Kṛṣṇa, grieves bitterly, O Saṃjaya.

sanskrit: dṛṣṭvā bhrātṝn hatān yuddhe bhīmasenena daṃśitān ātmāparādhāt sumahan nūnaṃ tapyati putrakaḥ
english: Seeing his mailed brothers slain in battle by Bhīmasena, my little son, surely, grieves exceedingly for his own transgression.

sanskrit: ko hi jīvitam anvicchan pratīpaṃ pāṇḍavaṃ vrajet bhīmaṃ bhīmāyudhaṃ kruddhaṃ sākṣāt kālam iva sthitam
english: For who that wished to live would advance against the Pāṇḍava Bhīma, of terrible weapons, enraged, standing there like Death made manifest?

sanskrit: vaḍavāmukhamadhyastho mucyetāpi hi mānavaḥ na bhīmamukhasaṃprāpto mucyeteti matir mama
english: A man set in the midst of the mare-mouthed fire beneath the sea might yet escape, but one who has come within Bhīma's reach cannot escape — such is my conviction.

sanskrit: na pāṇḍavā na pāñcālā na ca keśavasātyakī jānanti yudhi saṃrabdhā jīvitaṃ parirakṣitum
english: Neither the Pāṇḍavas, nor the Pāñcālas, nor Keśava and Sātyaki, when roused in battle, know how to guard their lives.

sanskrit: saṃjaya uvāca yat saṃśocasi kauravya vartamāne janakṣaye tvam asya jagato mūlaṃ vināśasya na saṃśayaḥ
english: Saṃjaya said: That you grieve, O Kaurava, now that the slaughter of folk is upon us — you yourself are the root of this world's destruction, there is no doubt.

sanskrit: svayaṃ vairaṃ mahat kṛtvā putrāṇāṃ vacane sthitaḥ ucyamāno na gṛhṇīṣe martyaḥ pathyam ivauṣadham
english: Having yourself stirred up this great enmity, and abiding by the word of your sons, though counseled you would not take the counsel, as a dying man refuses wholesome medicine.

sanskrit: svayaṃ pītvā mahārāja kālakūṭaṃ sudurjaram tasyedānīṃ phalaṃ kṛtsnam avāpnuhi narottama
english: Having yourself drunk down, O great king, the Kālakūṭa poison so hard to digest, now reap its fruit in full, O best of men.
